title: Simple app, nice features, very easy to follow through with
body:
You can only make three Habits at a time without paying, and yall have LOST your minds if you think I’m about to pay $99 for such basic functionality. 

That said, I think the limit is beneficial since it kept me from piling expectations onto myself. The process is simple enough that it’s never been overwhelming.

My favorite feature is that you can mark a “null” day, which doesn’t add to OR interrupt a streak. It’s nice for when one of my goals wasn’t possible that day, but I don’t want to let go of my streak. Having this in-between makes it so I never feel the need to lie (which is a quick way to lose motivation).

The visual feedback of marking a completed a habit is nice, especially with the bright colors. Your phone also makes a nice *click* vibration which I like. 
You can also view statistics for how often you follow through with your goals. No ads, and an account isn’t required, which is always a plus.

Overall, very satisfied

title: Give this smaller app a chance
body:
I’ve tried a lot of habit trackers, but there is almost always TOO much to fill in that it made me not want to use them. The process of filling everything in felt like it needed to be a habit in itself. 

My ADHD brain gets too distracted; I desperately wanted simplicity. After years, I’ve developed some great habits simply by using timers and reading Atomic Habits, which this app draws some concepts from. Now, I want to visualize this in a simple, easy-understand-visual for novice data folks like my wife or friends. So I turned to this app, (shout out r/dataisbeautiful). This app does just that. With intention and time, I’m excited to see what my visual will look like. Literally 3 click options:

-Did you do it? Tap.
-Did you do some of it? Tap.  Tap.
-Didn’t do it? Tap. Tap. Tap.

Obviously, there are things to fill out. But compared to others, IMO, set up is simple. Reminder options are available. There is even an option for breaking habits! 

Free to use, so I’ve testing with 3 habits and I’m very happy so far. It’s only 1/2, but so far, so good. 

Some improvements for this app, for me, would just be customizable user preferences. Specifically, visuals with fonts. I have unique reading needs so the ability to alter these helps a ton! This would help keep the app accessible for all. TY for your great app.

title: This app helped me change my life
body: When I came to realize that habits are one of the fundamental building blocks of achieving success on the vision I have for my life, my next thought was to find the best system for motivating me to do all my goals every day. I really struggle with consistency, but it’s precisely that lack of consistency that is the #1 limiting factor to me achieving my vision for my life. So I went looking for a habit tracking app that really nails the dopamine reward cycle and would help me be the most motivated and therefore consistent with my daily goals. In short: that app is Everyday. I encourage you to try it for free with just three goals, and once you realize like I did how valuable it is, then shell out the few bucks for the premium version. Best ROI on your money of pretty much anything in life I can think of. This app is really robust; the features for how you can set up your habits covers absolutely everything that you could want to track, and they have icons and visuals and the whole main screen is basically a visualization of how consistent you are becoming. And they’re leveraging gamification things to make it more effective. It’s truly the perfect app for this. Can’t recommend it more.

title: Good but missing some features I'd like...
body:
I have been searching for a visual tracking app like this for ages. I love the color and how it lets you see so many days/habits at once. There are a couple features I would like though.

1. Is there a way to reorded the way the habits appear in the list? For example, the first habit I made was 'code 10 mins' with a reminder at 1700. But then I made 'yoga 20 mins' with a reminder at 700. I wanted to reorder the habits so they appear in the list chornologically, but was unable to do so. My OCD got the better of me and I ended up deleting the first habit because I couldn't take them being out of order.

2. More color options! Or maybe sets? Like a pastels option. Or a neon options. I would totally splurge a buck 99 for a rain themed color pallete, or something seasonal and dumb.

3. A lower life time purchase price. I usually buy the lifetime option if I know I am going to use an app daily. But 99 dollars is pretty steep, so I ended up going for the yearly subscription. 69.99 and I probably would have paid if I liked the weekly trial (and it had some of the features I mentioned above.) Then you can make extra by releasing fun cosmetic stuff like color palettes, etc. People who are choosing your app are probably choosing it for the ascetics, so I'm sure you could make extra cash that way once you have lifetime subscribers.

All in all hopeful for more updates! This is the only visual habit tracker I've found. I was considering making my own!

title: Easily the Simplest Habit Tracking App
body:
This is literally the best app. There’s no fancy stuff here. Just a straightforward, beautifully designed interface for tracking your habits. You can set a time for each habit, or you can forego that option. And you can use their awesome color-coding system to categorize visually the different kinds of habits you want to tackle. 

For instance, for the bad habits I want to say I was able successfully to avoid, I use a forbidding RED. But for habits that connect to my value of Faith (like prayer and scripture reading), I use BLUE. For exercises like pushups: YELLOW, etc.

You get three habits with the free option. For the paid, you can track as many habits as you want. I paid $30 for the year, and I’m not disappointed. I will pay the lifetime $99 subscription if at the end of the year I’m as deeply satisfied as I am now.

Best app this guy has purchased, next to the Dwell app.

title: I recommend this habit tracker all the time
body: In the past I haven’t had any success with habit trackers. I have ADHD and most of them held my attention for a day or two, maybe a week, then I would miss some days, I would feel super guilty, and I didn’t want to open the app again. I’ve used this habit tracker for a year and counting, and I really don’t know why it is so different. It could be the ability to still ‘log’ the days you don’t do something. Instead of filling in the rectangle, it puts a triangle in that space, and that feels like neutral data instead of a personal failing. With this app I found out that I exercised 60% of the time, wrote 80% of the time, never went more than three days without flossing, and I have a ‘high energy’ day WAY more often than I think. In fact, I think this app allows me to live up to my values, because I can provide myself with regular proof—I am the person I want to be.

This extra price hike is most likely going to cause me to stop using it since it is a relatively simple app that I can’t justify paying more for than other apps that offer significantly more (even Discovery+ is only $4.99/month!). This is creeping up to be the cost of iTunes and compared to other apps, it’s no longer worth it for a simple app that is essentially a daily habit/to do list. Personally, I love the simplicity and it has been my favorite habit tracker but now that it’s more than “a cup of coffee”, it no longer seems like a fair price to be asking people to pay. I am certain that you’ll see more and more reviews like this one with your most recent price increase and will most likely end up losing customers.

If I could make a suggestion, please go back to $5/month (which I’ve been willing to pay) or make it a one time $30 lifetime cost which I’m sure many people will gladly pay. However, asking for almost $100 for lifetime is GREEDY and UNBELIEVABLE.

I use a lot of different tools for these experiments, and I really appreciate the care and attention that has gone into this app. I’m not always good at using it, but even if I’m only using it for a few months at a time, it’s really helpful in tracking what I can do easily, what I have resistance to, and what seems actually close to impossible. title: Greedy Ludicrous Pricing
body:
If you care about helping the most people possible and doing the most good possible, consider charging what most people will actually pay for a habit app. What’s more important, you making as much money as you can, or you making a bigger impact on the world and uplifting the collective quality of life on earth? Please consider. Thank you for making the app but it is unusable for me at this price range. $100 for a lifetime purchase. For an app that shows a colored tile when I click it? There’s so much more capable software people can buy for $100. Please consider this!

After reading other developer responses it seems the developer does want to help as many people as possible but is having trouble financing their ability to work in coding. 

Is there another solution besides jacking up the price of this 1 app to such high heights?

If you kept the features of this app the same and didn’t work much on it, your work-to-compensation ratio would even out over time even with the app at a lower price point. 

This would free you up to work on other apps/projects. 

If you only want to work on this project and see it as more of a luxury habit-tracking app that caters to richer customers, then alright, I guess I understand. There’s other reasonably priced habit-tracking apps we can use. 

I just have a problem with how many developers are going to subscription model to bleed customers of their money. It’s insane. Almost everything is a subscription now. And it’s not because it’s truly necessary. There’s so much greed now in software. 

There has to be another better way. 

By the way, if 100 different apps & services are trying to charge us the price of a coffee a month, what does that add up to? EVERYONE is trying to do it now.

body: I am now on day seven of using this gorgeous habit tracker, and I love it. The colors are pretty, and I find watching the streaks build very motivating. it syncs flawlessly -- and immediately -- across Chrome, iPhone, and Mac. (I haven't tried it on my watch yet.) I found out it could be set up to open in a fresh tab on Chrome, and it's the best thing ever because I am so frequently reminded of my daily habits and able to easily check them off when I'm ready. The week-long starter email series is very helpful, and the "Learn" tab has a wealth of information on setting and maintaining habits, with lots of scientific background about what works and why. I also had a question for the developer, and she got back to me quickly with a kind, helpful email. In the meantime, I had figured out how to solve the issue, but she mentioned that she would keep playing around with it so that others didn't have the same confusion. As a tip, if you change the colors a lot (as I do, since mine are in rainbow order, so I have to tweak things every time I move/add/archive a habit), the easiest way to do it is via the Chrome extension: hover over the habit name, then click on the color dot to the left and choose a new color.) After all, the beauty is part of the point of the app! (Developer: It would be great if it were this easy to change colors on the Mac app, but this is a good work-around and certainly not a deal-breaker!)

title: Great App, Too Expensive

Absurd!!!  1Password is a far more complex app with a whole development and support team behind it.

All of that said, Everyday is a nice app.  It's intuitive with great use of color, making it both easy to read and visually appealing.  I've had a few email exchanges with the developer and he is friendly and responsive.  I'd pay for the app if it were reasonably priced, but out of principal more than anything else, I refuse to subscribe at these prices.

*Response to the developer:  I agree with what you wrote regarding value.  So let's compare apples to apples.  Awesome Habits is $22.99 for a LIFETIME license.  Habit Tracker (by Davetech Co) is $4.99 for a LIFETIME license.  Each of these apps offers more features than Everyday.  Again, I'm not trying to be a jerk, but $30/year forever is ridiculous.

I blame Apple for that... greedy!

UPDATE: Developer responded below that the price had to go to because the app wasn’t sustainable. That’s the problem with many app developers today. They want to write one app, get customers, then raise the price. They’ve given up on making other apps and adding more value to draw in more customers. Instead, they’re exploiting their one success story and raising prices for the few who are willing to stick around. It’s happening over and over and over. $4 calendar utilities turning into $20 calendar utilities for a “polish” upgrade, turning into $30/year subscriptions - for a calendar utility.

At the end of the day, if you feel like an app that replicates what you can do with a spreadsheet is worth $60/year, go for it. But this sort of price jacking is ruining the App Store, slowly, through attrition. Maybe the balance sheets don’t yet reflect it, but they will.

I had to try out a few apps but this one is by far my favorite and it’s helping so much. It looks pretty and I do it everyday, the encouraging emails are nice. Would absolutely recommend this to anyone!!
author: Kreuzberg007

title: Useless unless you upgrade.
body: Beautiful app except the free version is useless- only lets you tract three habits. Unless you want to pay $30 for the upgraded version, don’t bother.
author: S 32_S

title: Simple and well designed habit tracker
body: I’ve been using Everyday to track a handful of habits related to my 2020 goals and have found it’s very simple and intuitive interface easy to use and keep track of my progress.
author: Matthew Tole

title: Glitch
body: My app is glitching, it says that I didn’t complete some of my habits when I did, and when I try to click and change it, it is stuck that way. I am unable to change the habit to completed, this has happened several times.

title: Simple, awesome
body: Only using the free version (so ltd to 3 habits). But 3 habits is a lot on some days! This app has actually been quite motivating with its simple pleasing visuals and stats. Once I’ve really begun to live and breathe these habits maybe will add a few more :)
author: Akrob23

title: Different. Better.
body: Have tried them all, but there’s something different about this one. Great graphic presentation coupled with really interesting info and science. Clearly a labor of love by its designer. Highly recommend!
author: sadfaced girl

title: Best Habit Tracker I have seen in the App Store
body:
The UX is amazing! It is elegant in it’s simplicity, hiding a full feature-set that is equal or better than any of the similar apps.

I have downloaded and tried nearly every habit tracker in the App Store all the way back to Chains.cc. EVERYDAY became my all time favorite in just a few days and I gladly subscribed to support its continued development.

1st habit to set up: Check into EVERYDAY every day! Also, be sure to review the “documentation”. Pure gold. I hope the developer continues to add to this section as I have a new habit to review this section.
author: Coachdan007

title: Unique
body: Let’s be honest... eye candy matters. If it didn’t, we’d all still be working from a command prompt on a monochrome display. Color and graphics make it so much easier to assimilate data and Everyday positively EXCELS at this. (Nothing to do with the MS spreadsheet app of the same name). Everyday runs smooth and stable on iPhone, iPad and the web (in fact, there’s more real estate for OCD types like me to fill on the web view). Added bonus: the dev eats his own dogfood - he includes a lot of surprisingly useful and inspirational content in the form of ‘documentation’. He’s also very responsive to comments and questions.
author: Left0verture

title: I dig it! Has helped make habits
body: It’s a smooth nice way to keep myself accountable.
author: snackattackpack

title: Amazing
body: It’s cliche but I really don’t write reviews ever. I’ve recently been testing 4 or 5 different habit trackers and then found this one and realized my search was over. It has worked flawlessly for me thus far and the user interface truly is gorgeous. I needed something that had a web UI since I spend most my time working with 4 monitors and this has worked great between my windows desktop, iPad, and iPhone. The bright sharp colors motivate me to stick to my habits in order to fill it up while the dark mode is nice and easy on my eyes. Also love the streak counters on the side so I can see them without having to go searching. Signed up for a year and it was worth every dollar.
author: Silentabyss26

title: Keeping me motivated everyday!
body: 95% of the apps I’ve downloaded in my life never get used more than a couple days. This one has lasted a week and I’m really enjoying it.
author: grggrzbm

title: Fantastic
body: Great app, helps me keep my habits going , s and I payed for the premium.
author: genco311

title: Pros & Cons
body:
1. It has a gorgeous interface and that is extremely inviting. 
2. Way overpriced. I would pay $5 once maybe, I don’t mind giving kickbacks to the creators, but the monthly or yearly cost for pro is exorbitant when there are so many free versions out there of similar design.
author: Mme.Abigail

title: Too expensive for the limited functionality
body: $4.99 a month is too much to ask for the ability to electronically check a box.
author: Sfmrunner

title: Helps me stay motivated!
body: This app helps me to feel accountable for keeping up with the tasks I need to meet my goals. I am only using the free app so I don’t know how much better the purchased app is.
author: S in OC

title: Inconsistent - needs an update
body: When you reorder a habit, it rarely puts it where you release it. Annoying. Habit titles could be a little wider on the main screen. No font control.
author: markgravitygood

title: Positive, Small Improvements
body:
I’m ADHD inattentive type and as such I need very visual cues for positive habit tracking. I like how simple this app is, especially to design habits that only occur on weekdays. Plus, the method of 1% improvements are backed scientifically.

I paid the subscription fee because it’s a great app with a developer who obviously cares. Keep doing good things!

title: So much better!!!
body: Wow, this app has gotten so much better. Thank you for working on it. And please, keep it up!

title: Amazing
body: I have done extensive research on habit trackers. This is the only app which is not only simple and beautiful but it’s accessible on your desktop as well. Truly groundbreaking.

body:
Title says it all. Thank you to the developer for not excluding the thousands of us still using our perfectly working older devices and OSes.

author: TheDeejay01

title: This App Is The Real Deal
body: $12 a year is a steal for the value of this habit tracker. I especially love how the new update improved the design (which was already 5-stars) and offered more statistics for me to see. The setup allows for “don’t skip twice” mentality which I find is a lot more sustainable than a “don’t break the chain/streaks mean everything” mentality that I see on some self-improvement apps.

title: Love this app
body: This has been a great habit builder!
author: J Cordle

title: Love it!
body: These habit tracker apps are great, because once you build up some momentum doing your habits every day, it becomes easier and easier to keep them up. I used to use a different one, but what I love about this one is that I can customize the colors so much, and it maintains a high score, so even if I “break the chain,” I have a goal to start shooting for again right away.
author: Max Jacobson

title: Love the app
body: I tried multiple habit tracking apps and this is by far the best and most intuitive. The tracking for picking up new habits and getting rid of old ones works.
author: Eightb1666

title: The only habit tracker that works for me.
body:
Everyday is beautifully designed. From the icons, to the simplistic UI, to the subtle color changes, it makes the experience easier to use.

Having a chrome extension in addition to the iPhone app is what allows me to consistently remind me of the important habits to complete each day. 

This app succeed where other streaks app fails for its simplicity and design. You have low over head, one click completion, and easy on the eyes. 

Worth the subscription for me.
